request.spec:
A sheet id entry and a button compare this sheet with another: one line per grade of this sheet,
<grade> <this sheet's summary due-total for the grade> <the other sheet's>, 0.00 for a grade the
other sheet has no one on; a sheet that does not exist gives no lines.

agent.result_text:
The sheet comparison is in place, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works:** a new "Compare sheets" panel on the home screen has a sheet id box (`compare-sheet`) and a Compare button (`compare`). Pressing Compare shows one `compare-line` for each grade, A, B and C, in the form `<grade> <this sheet's due-total> <the other sheet's>`.
- Each total is worked out the same way the Summary panel works out its per-grade due-total: retired people are left out, and so are amounts shown as n/a.
- A grade with no one on it in the other sheet shows 0.00.
- If the other sheet has never been used, no lines appear.
- Each press re-reads the other sheet, so changes another user made since the last comparison are included.

**Changes:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/exists` (`sheets/{sheetId}/exists.GET.yml` plus `sheet/RespondWithExists.java`), says whether a sheet exists. I needed it because the normal sheet-load request marks a sheet as existing. Looking up a missing sheet that way would have created it.
- **Front end:** a new file, `src/main/frontend/features/compare/compare.slot.tsx`.

The per-grade calculation is now copied in the compare panel as well as in the Summary panel, so a change to how the Summary counts would need making in both places.

The test reads the lines only 300 ms after pressing Compare. That was enough on every run here, but on a slow machine it could make the test fail now and then.
